objectives.text: Get Carriacou and Petite Martinique back on their feet after Hurricane Beryl (landfall 1 July 2024). Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell warned before landfall that Carriacou would take extreme damage and afterwards called the destruction there severe, with ninety percent of buildings reported destroyed (the figure as attributed in press reports to a CARICOM summit report, not yet checked against that report).

grand_strategy.reading: Grenada's strategy, as far as the sources read show it, is small-state survival through the regional bloc: CARICOM partners are its first call for relief and security, and its own means are a request for a helicopter, a storm-battered outer island and a passport it sells to investors. Its one clear external line in 2026 is to press diplomacy and sovereignty against the US operation in Venezuela, while Washington asks it for a security favour. Recovery from Beryl, not foreign policy, remains the binding constraint of 2024-26. Confidence C throughout: the Wikipedia index was read, but press summaries of July 2024 and January 2026 are the only sources opened, and the UK, the Taiwan switch, CARICOM as a bloc, the nutmeg and tourism economy and the Ukraine and Gaza positions are still open and unwritten.

stances.note: Cooperates on security while resisting the US line on Venezuela. Mitchell called the 3 January 2026 operation a push toward instability and said one state governing another has no place outside colonial relationships (the reluctance is in his words). The cooperation is a US request for a radar listening post on Grenada (reported by the Gleaner editorial; Grenada's answer is not in the sources read). Trend stable: no source shows a movement over time. Bond none: our reading of pure interest, C.
